To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gastric emptying in healthy preterm infants is rapid and that the gastric emptying pattern is not altered in infants who are born prematurely and have a birth weight less than or equal to 1,500 grams.
the gastric emptying of formula in preterm infants is regulated by the rate of gastric emptying and the rate of gastric secretion.
gastric emptying of breast milk is slower than formula and is associated with a greater incidence of gastric residual volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of gastric emptying in premature infants.
the regulation of the gastrointestinal tract, and specifically with the mechanisms that regulate gastric emptying.
the development of a novel, low cost and easy to use, device for the measurement of gastric emptying in premature babies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factors regulating gastric emptying of formula are not well understood, and are likely to be multifactorial.
there is a significant relationship between the level of education and the level of income of the people.
the use of a single formula for the management of the preterm infant is not justified and that a variety of different formulas should be made available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gastric emptying (GE) in preterm infants is regulated by a complicated system of neural and humoral factors that are influenced by the environment.
the results from our study suggest that the gastric emptying of preterm infants may be regulated by both the volume of the meal and the rate of gastric distension.
the regulation of gastric emptying in premature infants is multifactorial and is dependent on a complex interaction of gastric and post-gastric mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gastric emptying of breast milk is regulated by the infant's ability to coordinate sucking with swallowing.
we have developed a method to measure and predict gastric emptying of formula and breast milk.
